title: CcCommon constructor throws NullPointerException if no default toolchain is found

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

Trying to use cc_common.compile without a cc_toolchain from toolchain resolution or with a cc_toolchain from toolchain resolution after a host_platform transition make bazel throw exception

All referenced files are available in attached zip-file

b7d419bc09396eaf7e45aba529cbe2463824edaf_log.txt  [partial - full log in attachment]

    Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException
    	at com.google.common.base.Preconditions.checkNotNull(Preconditions.java:877)
    	at com.google.devtools.build.lib.rules.cpp.CcCommon.<init>(CcCommon.java:167)
    	at com.google.devtools.build.lib.rules.cpp.CcModule.compile(CcModule.java:1637)
    	at com.google.devtools.build.lib.bazel.rules.cpp.BazelCcModule.compile(BazelCcModule.java:91)

Git bisect reveals that this fault was introduced with the following patch:

    commit b2ae211e821f9b43fd59d52c71410572096b3c24 (refs/bisect/bad)
    Author: George Gensure <ggensure@uber.com>
    Date:   Wed Dec 11 05:43:11 2019 -0800

        Require non-null descriptions for MiddlemanActions
        
        Prevent an uninformative "null for <target>" name from being presented
        for MiddlemanAction prettyPrint by mandating a description not be null.
        Use a descriptive name for the CcCompilationHelper middleman based on
        the objc implementation, populated from CcCommon. Limit the objc
        interpretation within the helper to the matching objc purposes.
    
        Closes #10360.
    
        PiperOrigin-RevId: 284967632

Removing the offending null pointer check with the following patch fixes the issue;
branch: https://github.com/torgil/bazel/commits/10897_cc_common_nullpointer
diff: https://github.com/torgil/bazel/commit/7d79a245e5ca72ccef7ecff5920f4e3b5d76d024

## Feature requests: what underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?

Ability to choose toolchain with either host_platform transition or by passing it directly to rule from provider / attribute.

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

Unpack the attached zip-file and run:

    $  bazel build --incompatible_enable_cc_toolchain_resolution //:compile_fail

These files are relevant:

WORKSPACE

    workspace(name = "MyWorkspace")


BUILD.bazel

    load("@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:cc_toolchain_config.bzl", "cc_toolchain_config")
    load(":rules.bzl", "cc_compile_fail")
    
    filegroup(
        name = "empty",
        srcs = [],
    )
    
    cc_toolchain(
        name = "my_cc_toolchain",
        all_files = ":empty",
        ar_files = ":empty",
        as_files = ":empty",
        compiler_files = ":empty",
        dwp_files = ":empty",
        linker_files = ":empty",
        objcopy_files = ":empty",
        strip_files = ":empty",
        supports_param_files = 1,
        toolchain_config = ":local_linux",
        toolchain_identifier = "local_linux",
    )
    
    cc_toolchain_config(
        name = "local_linux",
        compiler = "compiler",
        cpu = "local",
        disable_static_cc_toolchains = False,
    )
    
    cc_compile_fail(
        name = "compile_fail",
        toolchain = ":my_cc_toolchain",
    )


rules.bzl

    hello_world = """\
    #include <stdio.h>
    int main(int argc, char *argv[])
    {
        printf("Compile me\\n");
        return 0;
    }
    """
    
    def _cc_compile_fail_impl(ctx):
        cc_toolchain = ctx.attr.toolchain[platform_common.ToolchainInfo]
        filename = ctx.label.name
        src = ctx.actions.declare_file(filename + ".c")
        ctx.actions.write(
            output = src,
            content = hello_world,
        )
    
        features = cc_common.configure_features(
            ctx = ctx,
            cc_toolchain = cc_toolchain,
            requested_features=[],
            unsupported_features=[],
        )
    
        (compilation_context, compilation_outputs) = cc_common.compile(
            name = filename + ".o",
            actions = ctx.actions,
            cc_toolchain = cc_toolchain,
            srcs = [src],
            feature_configuration = features,
            compilation_contexts = [],
        )
    
        return [
            DefaultInfo(files = depset(compilation_outputs.pic_objects)),
        ]
    
    cc_compile_fail = rule(
        implementation = _cc_compile_fail_impl,
        fragments = ['cpp'],
        attrs = {
            "toolchain": attr.label(
                mandatory = True,
            ),
        },
    )


### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

Ubuntu 18.04.4 LTS

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

Failure is seen on the following:
- development version   [ b7d419bc09396eaf7e45aba529cbe2463824edaf ]
- release 2.1.1
- release 2.2.0

### If `bazel info release` returns "development version" or "(@non-git)", tell us how you built Bazel.

Failing version:

    $ git checkout origin/master
    $ bazel-2.0.0 build src:bazel

Version with patch:

    $ git remote add torgil https://github.com/torgil/bazel.git
    $ git fetch torgil 10897_cc_common_nullpointer
    $ git checkout 10897_cc_common_nullpointer
    $ bazel-2.0.0 build src:bazel
